{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Immediately after the election, Wall Street-backed foundations such as Third Way and the Concord Coalition organized a “Campaign to Fix the Debt” to spin the election results as a mandate for a “bi-partisan” focus on reducing the deficit as the highest national priority.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"For decades, billionaire Pete Peterson has funded groups that claim that the universal entitlement programs Social Security and Medicare are bankrupting the nation and that their future growth must thus be drastically trimmed.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"In 2011, the Simpson-Bowles Congressional Commission put to a vote a long-term “budget compromise” that would have instituted three times as much in budget cuts than in tax increases.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Despite President Obama’s evident willingness to reach a one-sided budget compromise, Tea Party insistence on no tax increases, even on the wealthiest, scuttled the deal.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The “resolution” of the manufactured, alleged “budget crisis” was to postpone a decision on further deficit reduction until the end of 2012, resulting in the contrived “fiscal cliff”.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]}],"unresolved_references":[]}

{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Immediately after the election, Wall Street-backed foundations such as Third Way and the Concord Coalition organized a “Campaign to Fix the Debt” to spin the election results as a mandate for a “bi-partisan” focus on reducing the deficit as the highest national priority.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"For decades, billionaire Pete Peterson has funded groups that claim that the universal entitlement programs Social Security and Medicare are bankrupting the nation and that their future growth must thus be drastically trimmed.",
